title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: GOAL’s ICSP programme in Sierra Leone has supported project participants including women, youth and vulnerable groups to enhance their capabilities and resilience to shocks and stresses. ICSP interventions addressed the multidimensional poverty issues communities have historically been faced with. GOAL uses systems strengthening approaches in Health, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) and Blue Economy interventions. There is a particular focus on interventions to enable children U5 and youth and women of childbearing age to access quality, responsive services in the health system. ICSP focuses on communities and the enabling environment (including rules and regulations), as well as the supporting functions such as access to technology, finance, skills, etc. Systemic and integrated approaches enabled by ICSP helped GOAL reach a total of 770,194 people in 2024. The integration and overlay of the ICSP programme interventions with other activities has helped GOAL to deepen and sustain impact on the communities it works with. Moreover, a very small pilot programme in the Blue Economy sector using ICSP resources resulted in catalytic funding beyond ICSP in the same sector.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Outcome 2: People Have Resilient Health. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: Building resilience to shocks that impact health, such as disease outbreaks through a focus on Early Warning and Response Systems (EWRS) by working in collaboration with the NDMA. The findings of a gender analysis are informing the planning and implementation of disease outbreak preparedness and response interventions, ensuring that they are gender-responsive and inclusive.
